conflict: Directory sources only. Reported non-active since September 2024 and cogaid.com returns HTTP 500.

name: Biosemi
evidence: Company About page: the founders worked over a decade at the Medical Physics department, University of Amsterdam, then decided to start BioSemi in 1998

name: MazeEngineers
evidence: Crunchbase gives 2012, founder Shuhan He, Cambridge MA
conflict: AGGREGATOR-ONLY. The company own /our-company/ page now 404s and mazeengineers.com redirects to conductscience.com/mazeengineers — it is a product line under the ConductScience brand rather than a standalone company.

name: Bee Medic
evidence: Company site: Since 2005, BEE Medic GmbH has been developing high-end systems for non-invasive neurotherapy and diagnostics
conflict: The company history page traces a lineage through EEG Spectrum (1988, Sue and Siegfried Othmer), EEG Info Inc (2003) and BEE Systems Switzerland (2004). Those are predecessors and affiliates, not the founding of BEE Medic GmbH.

name: PENTAS
evidence: Company history page: established July 2015 in Shibuya, Tokyo as Allm Inc medical-equipment subsidiary. PENTAS IS A COMPANY, not a product as the stored URL suggested.
conflict: In April 2025 it was excluded from Allm consolidated subsidiaries and moved into the GENARK Inc group — a change of ownership, not a founding. pentas.allm.net now redirects to pentas-medical.jp, consistent with that separation.

name: Cortech Solutions
evidence: Company About page, verbatim: Cortech was founded in September of 2001

name: Ornim Medical
evidence: Tracxn and CB Insights give 2004, founders Michal Balberg and Revital Shechter
conflict: AGGREGATOR-ONLY and the company appears defunct: ornim.com now redirects to a HugeDomains for-sale parking page. The 2011 GE healthymagination and OrbiMed $20M event that dominates search results is a Series B, not a founding.

name: BrainFx
evidence: Crunchbase, Tracxn and PitchBook agree on 2012; founders Tracy Milner and Heather Condello
conflict: AGGREGATOR-ONLY. brainfx.com is live but states no founding year and its About URLs 404. A ventureLAB profile notes the founders ran an Ontario occupational-therapy practice from 2008 — a predecessor practice, not BrainFx.

name: C8 Sciences
evidence: PitchBook, CB Insights and Gust give April 2011, New Haven CT
conflict: AGGREGATOR-ONLY. The company own About and founder pages describe Bruce Wexler Yale research and an NIH grant but give no founding year. One review site claims a first product in 2010, which would predate the company date.

name: Brainbit Inc.
evidence: CB Insights, Tracxn and LeadIQ all give 2015; LeadIQ adds founder Boris Goldstein
conflict: AGGREGATOR-ONLY. The company About page states no founding year and its only date signal is a copyright reading 2016-2026, which sits uneasily with 2015. LOCATION also conflicts: our index says New York, the company site says headquarters in California with an office in Poland and manufacturing in China.

name: Clearhead
evidence: Company About page: Clearhead was born in 2018 when medical doctor Angela Lim joined forces with software engineer Michael Connolly. Corroborated by University of Auckland CIE newsroom.
conflict: clearhead.org.nz now redirects to myclearhead.com.

name: Elevatr
evidence: Gust self-submitted profile: founded January 2017, New York, co-founders Israel Zyskind and Aaron Rozzi
conflict: AGGREGATOR-ONLY, and elevatr.com NO LONGER BELONGS TO THIS COMPANY — it now serves a German-language hospitality media and events platform. The Brooklyn app appears defunct and the domain repurposed.

name: Garlew
evidence: Company archived homepage, verbatim: Founded in 2014, and rooted in hundreds of years of psychological and sociological study. Co-founders Gerard Lebar Jr and Eric Lewandowski, Dallas TX.
conflict: Read from the Wayback Machine because garlew.com no longer resolves. The company appears defunct.

name: Akili Interactive
evidence: PureTech Health founded Akili Interactive Labs in 2011 as a Founded Entity, on cognitive-training technology licensed from Adam Gazzaley lab at UCSF
conflict: Went public via SPAC Aug 2022 as Akili Inc (Nasdaq AKLI), then ACQUIRED by Virtual Therapeutics via tender offer completed 1 July 2024 at $0.4340/share. Not a wind-down, as I had suggested in the brief.

name: Carl Zeiss
evidence: ZEISS own history page: in 1846, Carl Zeiss opened a workshop for precision mechanics and optical instruments in Jena, specifically 17 November 1846. The 175 Years of ZEISS anniversary in 2021 is arithmetically consistent.

name: Oura
evidence: Company blog history: began in 2013 in Oulu, Finland, founded by Petteri Lahtela, Kari Kivela and Markku Koskela. The first-generation ring came later via Kickstarter, so 2013 is founding rather than product launch.

name: PrecisionNeuroscience
evidence: Founded 2021 by Benjamin Rapoport, a Neuralink founding member, with Michael Mager, Demetrios Papageorgiou and Mark Hettick; Wikipedia cites STAT News July 2022 and CNBC corroborates in Jan 2023
conflict: This row is the DUPLICATE of Precision Neuroscience already identified by the dedup audit — the two names hash to different UUIDv5 ids.

name: Sleepio
evidence: Sleepio is the PRODUCT; the company is Big Health, co-founded by Peter Hames and Prof Colin Espie of Oxford. Investor and aggregator profiles give 2010.
conflict: AGGREGATOR-ONLY. Neither Big Health About page, the Sleepio Wikipedia article nor two press boilerplates state a founding year. A 2014 TechCrunch piece implies the idea originated around 2009 and Wikipedia dates the Sleepio launch to 2012; neither is a founding claim. OUR ROW IS NAMED AFTER THE PRODUCT.

name: Ginger
evidence: MIT Sloan: mental health has been at the heart of Ginger vision since it launched in 2011. Founded by Anmol Madan and Karan Singh out of the MIT Media Lab, commercialising Madan passive-mobile-sensing research.
conflict: Merged with Headspace in 2021 to form Headspace Health. 2011 is the original founding.

name: MyndVR
evidence: Fierce Healthcare: MyndVR began in 2016, founded by Chris Brickler and Shawn Wiora. Tracxn, PitchBook and Dealroom concur.
conflict: The company own site publishes no year, and myndvr.com now redirects to myndimmersive.com — a rebrand to Mynd Immersive, not a new founding.

name: BioMind
evidence: The legal entity behind BioMind is Hanalytics Pte Ltd, UEN 201706114W, incorporated in Singapore 5 March 2017; the UEN prefix encodes the registration year. Founders Raymond Moh and Zhenzhou Wu.
conflict: This is an INCORPORATION date standing in for a founding date. OUR ROW IS NAMED AFTER THE PRODUCT — the company is Hanalytics. The BioMind neuroimaging product launched publicly in 2018 with Beijing Tiantan Hospital.

name: Applied Brain Research
evidence: Secondary sources most often give 2013 as the founding year for this University of Waterloo spin-out from the Centre for Theoretical Neuroscience, makers of Nengo.
conflict: Three-way. The Canadian federal register records incorporation on 18 Sep 2012 (corporation 8299072). Secondary sources say founded 2013. At least one gives 2014 as the launch year. appliedbrainresearch.com/about is a 404, so the company itself does not arbitrate.

name: Facerehab
evidence: The Recursive: "In 2019, Veronika founded a digital rehabilitation therapy app for face palsy (paralysis) patients, FaceRehab."
conflict: The Recursive says 2019; a LinkedIn-derived mirror says 2020. Either founded 2019 and incorporated 2020, or the journalist erred. Not resolved.

name: Tactx Medical
evidence: PitchBook lists Tactx Medical, also known as PRODUXX, Inc., as founded in 2003 in Campbell, California.
caveat: Aggregator only. The primary source, the Creganna acquisition release of January 2010, states no founding year. The aggregator ties the name to PRODUXX, Inc., so 2003 may date Produxx rather than Tactx. The company has not existed independently since 2010.

name: Cyberonics
evidence: International Directory of Company Histories: "In December 1987 he and Zabara incorporated Cyberonics." Key Dates gives "1987: Cyberonics is founded." Founders Jacob Zabara, who originated vagus nerve stimulation, and Reese S. Terry.
caveat: Founding and incorporation coincide in December 1987. The company merged with Sorin S.p.A. on 19 Oct 2015 to form LivaNova and no longer exists under this name.

name: Concrn
evidence: Fast Forward, the nonprofit-tech accelerator, writing about its own cohort: "The founding team launched Concrn in 2014, a mobile 911 alternative for neighbors in crisis." Co-founders Jacob Savage and Doug Marks.
caveat: The source says "launched", which is close to but not identical with founding. Coverage thins after 2018 and current operating status is unconfirmed.

name: SensoMedical
evidence: Company about page: "SENSOMEDICAL was established by Maroun Farah in 2014." PitchBook independently agrees on both the year and the founder.

name: ElMindA
evidence: Company-authored boilerplate: founded in 2006 by Professor Amir Geva to objectively assess brain health. Consistent across ISRAEL21c and the Jewish Virtual Library, all tracing the company to Ben-Gurion University research.
caveat: The release announces a $28M Series C in November 2015; that is a funding event, not the founding. Substantial coverage stops around 2018 and current status is unconfirmed.

name: Synappse Assist
evidence: Crunchbase gives March 2017, founder Alexandre Valverde, Sao Paulo.
caveat: Aggregator only. No company about page and no Brazilian CNPJ registry record was found to corroborate the year.

name: foc.us
evidence: Aggregators give 2012 for this London developer of consumer tDCS headsets; founder Michael Oxley.
caveat: Aggregator only; no company page states a year. The site says foc.us is owned and operated by Brain Control Co., so the legal entity may be a company this index never names. The 2013 date in press coverage is the gamer headset launch, not a founding.

name: Medlink Neurology
evidence: Boilerplate reproduced across sources: "MedLink Corporation, founded in 1992, is the publisher of MedLink Neurology."
caveat: medlink.com returned 403 to direct fetches, so the year comes from search-indexed copies of the about page plus consistent third-party repetition rather than a page read directly.

name: XEED
evidence: Crunchbase gives 2016, Philadelphia, co-founders Sade Oba and Alfredo Muniz. Corroborated circumstantially: both were Penn Engineering seniors (EAS 2016) who won the inaugural 2016 President Innovation Prize, and TechCrunch covered them in July 2016 as a Penn students startup.
caveat: The Penn prize page does not itself state a founding year, so the exact figure rests on the aggregator.

name: FraSen
evidence: PitchBook lists FraSen, Inc. of Seoul as founded 2010; a smart sleep mask with brainwave sensors and bone-conduction audio.
caveat: Aggregator only, and frasen.com is now a HugeDomains parking page. With roughly four employees and no recent news the company appears defunct. Treat 2010 as unconfirmed.

name: SensPD LTD
evidence: Crunchbase gives 2017, founder Raffi Rembrand, Bosmat Tivon, Israel. Screens newborns for autism by repurposing standard oto-acoustic-emission hearing-screening hardware.
caveat: Founder Raffi Rembrand is described as an independent researcher since 2000; that is a biography date and is not the company founding. Startup Nation Central and the CORDIS grant record corroborate the company exists but neither was readable for a founding year.

name: Babbly
evidence: BetaKit: "Founded in 2018 by Maryam Nabavi (CEO) and Carla Margalef Bentabol (CTO)."
caveat: The article reports a $3.2M CAD seed round closed March 2022 and an app launch in 2020; neither is the founding.

name: Tovertafel (Active Cues)
evidence: "the first Tovertafel officially entered the care market in 2015, the same year that Anderiesen-Le Riche founded the company that would commercialize this system." The company was Active Cues, out of her TU Delft PhD research.
conflict: Crunchbase says 2014. The company own about page says only "Our first Tovertafel was launched in 2015", which is a product launch and not a founding. 2014 against 2015 is unresolved.

name: AgenT
evidence: Gust: "cofounded in March 2018 by Jerome Braudeau along with Baptiste Billoir." myfrenchstartup gives creation 2018 with SIREN 838187318, a block consistent with 2018 French registration.
conflict: One source states the founders launched AgenT in 2016. The 2018 figure may be incorporation rather than founding, with 2016 the year the project began. agent-biotech.com/about-us.html is a 404 so the company does not arbitrate.

name: CerebraCell
evidence: Parent site: "CerebraCell formed in 2015 and is focused on brain regeneration utilizing bioelectric stimulation and a re-fillable micro infusion pump."
caveat: Not an independent company. It is a portfolio venture of Leonhardt Ventures LLC, which spins out single-indication bioelectric companies from a shared patent estate. cerebracell.com states no founding year of its own, and the site disclaims that its products are unproven and not available for sale.

name: Sonovum
evidence: Saxon state media service: "2011 gegruendet, arbeitet das Unternehmen mit 16 Mitarbeitern an der Entwicklung und Erprobung einer neuartigen Technologie zur schnelleren und trennschaerferen Diagnose von Schlaganfaellen."
caveat: Founded as Sonovum AG, now trading as Sonovum GmbH, Leipzig HRB 37040. The current site states a product launch of Q4 2026, so the company remains pre-commercial on its current intracranial-pressure product despite a 2017 CE mark on the earlier acoustocerebrography device.

name: Biocross
evidence: Described as established in 2005 as a spin-off of the CSIC, with a stated foundation date of 26 January 2005.
caveat: The precision of 26 January 2005 suggests this is the Spanish mercantile registry incorporation date rather than a founding. biocross.es/about contains no founding year and the AseBio directory entry is behind a login.

name: Hubly Surgical
evidence: Company boilerplate: "Founded in 2019, Hubly Surgical is a medical device company with a mission to improve patient outcomes and quality of care for surgical procedures... starting with bedside cranial surgery."
caveat: A Northwestern University student spinout from The Garage accelerator, based in Chicago and Evanston, Illinois. The index records San Francisco, for which no support was found.

name: Bionen Medical Devices
evidence: Company history page: "The first company made its first debut in 1984 ... In 1989 BIONEN was born, specialized in design, production and marketing of medical devices for neurophysiopathology."
conflict: Third-party profiles including a MEDICA exhibitor listing say "Founded in 1984". The company own page distinguishes a 1984 predecessor venture by founder Carlo Nencioni from BIONEN itself, created 1989. Both are defensible depending on whether the predecessor counts.

name: BeHapbee
evidence: Audited consolidated financial statements: incorporated 3 January 2019 under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), formerly named Elevation Technologies, Inc., renamed Hapbee Technologies, Inc. in May 2020.
conflict: Aggregators variously give 2019, 2020 and 2004. Only 2019 has a filing behind it, but that filing records incorporation under a different name, and no independent statement of when the Hapbee venture itself began was found.

name: Bio-Signal Technologies
evidence: Crunchbase, ZoomInfo and Dealroom give October 2016 for Bio-Signal Technologies, LLC.
caveat: The about page is a 404 and the live site states no founding year, no history and no address. Its copy reads as translated boilerplate referring to domestic universities and tertiary hospitals, which suggests a US sales arm for a Chinese neurophysiology-equipment manufacturer rather than an originating developer. No primary source found.

name: Imagilys
evidence: Company anniversary page: "On July 18, 2005, we founded Imagilys." Founder and CEO Dr. Laurent Hermoye; BrainMagix neuroimaging software for neurosurgical planning.
caveat: Some aggregators say 2004; the company own explicit date wins. Do not derive a year from the anniversary number: the page slug says 15th while its heading says 17th, because it has been re-edited over time.

name: CubeHX
evidence: Tracxn lists CubeHX as founded 2018 in Montreal by Sylvain Senecal and Neil Fleischer.
caveat: Tracxn alone. The company no longer exists independently: cubehx.com redirects to leger360.com/cube-ai, Leger took a minority stake in 2022 and announced acquisition of 51% on 12 March 2024. The Leger release names the developers but gives no founding year.

name: Healing Hand Tech
evidence: Company-issued release dated 12 September 2023: "Established in 2020 and currently in its early stages, the company is diligently crafting a functional system prototype."
conflict: Tracxn says 2018; Crunchbase records 12 June 2020. The company own 2023 release says 2020, agreeing with Crunchbase against Tracxn. 2020 may also be the incorporation date rather than the start of the venture; the release does not distinguish.

name: Phobious
evidence: Corporate profile hosted by Fundacion Telefonica: "ANO DE FUNDACION: 2013". Established July 2013 by physics classmates Xavier Palomer and Dani Roig, VR exposure therapy for phobias.
conflict: Dealroom and Crunchbase-derived summaries give 2014. Spanish primary-adjacent sources consistently say 2013 and the founding narrative supports it, but the disagreement is unresolved.

name: Psious
evidence: Same company as the Phobious row: Phobious was renamed Psious. Fundacion Telefonica profile gives founding year 2013, founders Xavier Palomer and Dani Roig.
conflict: Dealroom and Crunchbase give 2014. Separately, this row and "Phobious" are the same company under two names and one of them should not exist.

name: Synergetics USA
evidence: Retina Today: "Synergetics was founded in August, 1991, as a designer and manufacturer of microsurgical instruments initially focused on vitreoretinal and subretinal ophthalmic procedures." Founders Kurt W. Gampp and Gregg D. Scheller.
conflict: The name "Synergetics USA" dates only from the 2005 reverse merger with Valley Forge Scientific, after which it traded as NASDAQ: SURG. 1991 is the founding of the operating business; 2005 created the named public entity.

name: Mindable Health
evidence: German healthcare trade press dates the founding explicitly to April 2019.
conflict: Startbase states a founding year of 2018. A Handelsregister lookup for Mindable Health GmbH would settle it. Not resolved.

name: Neuroverse
evidence: Gizmodo: "Based in La Jolla, California, Neuroverse was founded in 2012 by Salk Institute neuroscientist Ricardo Gil-da-Costa (now Neuroverse CEO) and the University of California, San Diego's Todd Coleman."
caveat: The company site confirms Gil-da-Costa co-founded it but states no year, hence the news citation. Public activity appears thin in recent years and current status is unconfirmed.

name: Cerenion
evidence: OuluHealth, the regional health innovation ecosystem body: "Founded in 2017 in Oulu." A University of Oulu spin-off; product C-Trend applies machine learning to standard EEG to quantify brain function in intensive care.
caveat: Tracxn records a first funding round in February 2018, which is consistent with a 2017 founding and is not itself a founding date.

name: Calm
evidence: "Calm was established on May 4, 2012 by Michael Acton Smith and Alex Tew." Corroborated by the founders' own interviews.
caveat: The company help-centre page returned 403, hence the encyclopedia citation. SCOPE: a consumer meditation and sleep subscription app with no hardware, neural interface or biosignal acquisition.

name: Nanology Labs
evidence: Dealroom, Crunchbase and PitchBook give 2018. A University of Toronto article notes "Since June 2018, Nanology Labs has picked up significant funding support", which corroborates the window without stating a founding year.
caveat: Aggregator only; the University of Toronto piece never states a founding year and was not used as the source. The company has since been renamed QurCan Therapeutics Inc.

name: EndoSpan
evidence: PitchBook and Tracxn both give 2009, founders Alon Shalev and Rafi Benary, Herzliya.
caveat: endospan.com has no history page and states no founding year; its only date is a copyright footer, which was not used. Hints of 2008 appear in aggregator-adjacent listings and could not be checked. Acquired by Artivion in May 2026.

name: Triumf Health
evidence: Company about page: "Kadri Haljas founded Triumf Health in October 2016, driven by her passion for mental health innovation and her extensive background in child psychology."
caveat: Origin is Estonian, founded in Tartu county; the Helsinki location in the index is a later registered seat rather than where it started.

name: Sooma Medical
evidence: Company about page: "Sooma Medical (Sooma Oy) is a Finnish medical device manufacturer established in 2013." Transcranial direct current stimulation devices for depression and chronic pain.
caveat: The wording is "established", read here as founding. The Finnish trade register was not consulted, so this is not an incorporation date.

name: Epitech
evidence: VentureRadar gives 2015 and lists epitechmag.com as the company website. Crunchbase and PitchBook agree on 2015.
conflict: Dealroom gives 2016. No primary source resolves it.

name: Brain Science Tools
evidence: Founder Bas Neggers in the first person on the company's own domain: "I founded the startup company Brain Science Tools BV in November 2011 as a spinoff from UMC Utrecht."
caveat: This is a team biography page, normally refused as a source. The exception is that it is an explicit first-person founding statement on the company's own site, not an incidental date in a blurb.

name: Brain.fm
evidence: Company about page: "Started as a focus-music company in 2014." Corroborated by Inc., which reports founders Adam Hewett and Junaid Kalmadi meeting at a conference in 2014.
caveat: Co-founder Hewett's earlier separate company Transparent dates to 2003 and appears in the same sources; that year is not Brain.fm's. SCOPE: an audio subscription with a neuroscience rationale, no device and no neural recording.

name: Advantis
evidence: EU-Startups reports Advantis Medical Imaging as founded in 2016 after roughly five years of research in advanced neuroimaging, with offices in Athens and Eindhoven.
caveat: The article body returned 403 so this rests on the search-index summary. The company was formerly named TomoTECH, so 2016 may date the earlier name or the rebrand. advantis.io has no about page and the Elevate Greece registry entry carries no founding year.

name: Swap
evidence: Company about page: "Swap GPS voit le jour en 2014 a l'occasion d'un concours d'entrepreneuriat sponsorise par le Credit Agricole." Founder Guillaume Eberwein, a biomedical engineering student at Ecole des Mines de Saint-Etienne.
conflict: A November 2016 article by La Fabrique Hexagonale was summarised as "created in 2016". That looks like the article's own publication year bleeding into the summary, and the company's own page plus several French outlets give 2014.

name: ZAPIENS
evidence: Asturian regional tech-cluster press: "Zapiens, fundada en 2014." Founders Daniel Suarez Sanchez and Samuel Ordieres, Oviedo.
caveat: A founder interview describes 2014 as when the idea was seeded rather than when the company came into existence; the AsturTIC piece states it as the founding year. zapiens.ai refused connections so its own wording could not be checked. SCOPE: enterprise knowledge-management AI, not neurotechnology.

name: Sensae
evidence: The Hub, a Danish startup platform, lists founding year 2020 for the Copenhagen company combining neuroscience, psychology and haptics in biofeedback for stress and anxiety.
caveat: Aggregator only; no company page, news article or accelerator announcement states a year. The website in the index is wrong: sensae.co now serves an unrelated UK perfume brand. The Hub lists the company site as sensae.com.

name: Mensior
evidence: CB Insights: founded 2015, Milan; an EEG-sensor application measuring mental activity for consumer and business use.
caveat: Aggregator only, and mensior.com does not resolve. No registry record for Mensior S.r.l. was found. The 2015 date coincides with the Imperial College Smart Helmet EEG publications and the product shares that name, so the year may be a confusion rather than a fact.

name: NBT Analytics
evidence: Company site: "NBT Analytics BV is a spin-off company from the VU Amsterdam. The company was founded in August 2015 by Dr. Klaus Linkenkaer-Hansen and Dr. Simon-Shlomo Poil." EEG biomarker analysis for CNS drug development.

name: Ginger Tiger
evidence: Startup Nation Finder lists Ginger Tiger as founded 2013 in Tel Aviv by Orna Altman; Tracxn and Crunchbase agree.
caveat: The company's own about page states no founding year at all, and the Startup Nation Central page returned 403 so it was read only through the search index. SCOPE: special-needs educational software with no EEG, BCI or neural interface.

name: Stroke Medical
evidence: CB Insights gives 2016; independent Chinese industry sources describe the company as established in 2016.
caveat: The row name is a nickname taken from the domain. The company is Shanghai HeartCare Medical Technology Corporation Limited, listed in Hong Kong as 6609.HK, making neuro-interventional devices for stroke. strokemedical.com refused HTTPS connections, so the year rests on databases rather than the company or its HKEX prospectus.

name: SpinTech Imaging
evidence: Company boilerplate in its own Series A release: "SpinTech MRI was founded 2017 by internationally recognized MRI industry professionals."
caveat: Now trades as SpinTech MRI, Bingham Farms, Michigan; acquired MR Innovations in February 2021. It has close Wayne State University research ties but no source describes it as a formal spin-off, so it is not recorded as one.

name: Nextstem
evidence: Inc42: "In 2020, while the duo was still in college, they set up Nexstem." Founders Siddhant Dangi and Deepansh Goyal, BITS Pilani alumni; non-invasive BCI headset and developer stack.
conflict: Location only, not the year: Inc42 and other outlets place the company in Bengaluru while the index says Gurugram. The name is also misspelled in the index; the company is Nexstem, matching nexstem.ai.

name: Explorer Research
evidence: Acquisition announcement of December 2023, echoed by Research Live and the Insights Association: Explorer Research was "established in 2002", with offices in Toronto and Chicago.
caveat: The company site has no about page and states no founding year, so this rests on acquisition coverage. Acquired by Savanta, part of Next 15 Group plc, in December 2023, and still trading under its own brand.

name: Lifelines Neurodiagnostic Systems
evidence: Company founders page: "Lifelines Neurodiagnostic Systems, Inc. was founded July 1, 2001."
conflict: Aggregators variously give 2000 and 1999. 2000 is when Simon Griffin left MEDICA in Dusseldorf and decided to start the business, which is pre-founding; 1999 belongs to Lifelines Ltd of the UK, a separate earlier company founded by Dave Hulin and Stephen Walters. The US entity in this row is 2001.

name: Ola Mundo Inc.
evidence: "Ola Mundo (Hello World in Portuguese) was created in January 2012 as a by-parents-for-parents project." Founders Ofir Harel and Alex Pavtoulov.
caveat: A company-issued release rather than independent reporting, and January 2012 dates the parent project, which may predate incorporation. Crunchbase marks the company permanently closed. SCOPE: assistive communication software, not a device acting on the nervous system.

name: Imeka
evidence: Canada Economic Development for Quebec Regions, July 2023: "Founded in 2011 by two Universite de Sherbrooke professors and researchers, Imeka specializes in imaging white matter of the brain." Co-founders Maxime Descoteaux and Pierre-Marc Jodoin.
caveat: A Government of Canada release distributed via Newswire; the canada.ca original returned 403. Imeka's own about page gives no founding year, only a founder-biography line that was not used.

name: ADmit Therapeutics
evidence: IDIBELL newsroom: ADmit Therapeutics was "founded at the end of 2017 as a spin-off from the Bellvitge Biomedical Research Institute (IDIBELL)." Other coverage narrows this to December 2017.
caveat: SCOPE: despite the name it is neither a device company nor a drug developer. MAP-AD is an epigenetic blood test with an algorithm that stratifies mild cognitive impairment patients by probability of progressing to Alzheimer's dementia. CAP lab accreditation November 2024.

name: Rewellio
evidence: tech2b, the Upper Austrian public startup incubator, lists Rewellio GmbH as founded 2017, founders Georg Teufl and Bernhardt Kern, Bad Ischl. Corroborated by NR Times, which reports Teufl founded it after working as a stroke therapist.

name: Neurallys
evidence: Tendance Ouest: "l'entreprise n'est fondee qu'en 2016 au sein de la faculte de medecine de Caen." Co-founders Philippe Auvray, Lionel Rousseau and Prof. Philippe Cornu.
caveat: An implantable intracranial-pressure sensor for hydrocephalus shunt patients. neurallys.com refused connection and may be dead. LOCATION: founded in Caen and moved HQ and R&D to Colombelles in Normandy in 2017; the index records Paris, which reflects only its incubation at the Institut du Cerveau.

name: Marigold Health
evidence: Aggregator profiles give 2016, founders Shrenik Jain and Ravi Shah. CB Insights still files the company under the slug sunrise-health.
conflict: Some listings say 2017. The company renamed twice — it began as a Johns Hopkins student project called Beacon in the 2016-17 Social Innovation Lab cohort, became Sunrise Health, covered by TechCrunch in May 2017, and is now Marigold Health. 2016 is the Beacon origin and 2017 the Sunrise Health launch, which is exactly why the two circulate.

name: Invention Labs
evidence: "In 2007, this group of IIT Madras alumni formally incorporated Invention Labs Engineering Products Private Limited, an IIT Madras incubated company." Founder Ajit Narayanan.
caveat: The wording is "formally incorporated", so this is strictly an incorporation date. The live brand is Avaz Inc; inventionlabs.in is legacy and its about page returns a 500. The Avaz AAC app launched February 2010, which is a product launch and a likely trap in aggregator data.

name: aidoc
evidence: Company about page: "Established in 2016, Aidoc's solutions first focused on aiding radiologists in reducing turnaround time and increasing quality and efficiency by flagging acute anomalies in real time." Founders Elad Walach, Michael Braginsky and Guy Reiner.
caveat: SCOPE: a general clinical-AI and radiology triage platform with 18+ FDA-cleared algorithms across many body systems, covering by its own account 75% of a facility's patient population. It qualifies for a neurotechnology index only through its neurovascular products, a minority of the portfolio.

name: CortiCare
evidence: Crunchbase, Tracxn, Dealroom and CB Insights all give 2009, founder Brad Westcott, Carlsbad.
conflict: The company's own Mission and History page presents a timeline beginning in 2012 and never states a founding year or names a founder, so its own history is silent on 2009. The HCAP Partners 2019 release says only that an acquisition target, Physician Ancillary Services LLC, was founded 2008.

name: BrainVoyager
evidence: Maastricht Health Campus profile: "Founded in 2000 by Rainer Goebel when he joined Maastricht University as Professor of Cognitive Neuroscience."
caveat: The row is a product name. BrainVoyager is software; the company is Brain Innovation B.V. of Maastricht. Goebel began developing BrainVoyager at the Max Planck Institute in Frankfurt in the mid-1990s, so the software predates the company by several years and that earlier date must not leak in as a founding year.

name: Mundo Pato
evidence: Crunchbase, ZoomInfo, CB Insights and RocketReach all give 2010, founder Cesar Pachon, Portland Oregon.
caveat: The company about page states no founding year, so 2010 rests entirely on aggregators. mundopato.com serves UnitusTI, the customer-facing brand; the row is named after the holding company. SCOPE: a data-collection and curriculum SaaS for ABA therapy and special-needs education, not neurotechnology.

name: SensArs
evidence: Swiss commercial register: SensArs Neuroprosthetics Sarl entered in the trade register 12 June 2014, statutes established 5 June 2014, UID CHE-130.906.673, Lausanne. Corroborated by Venturelab calling it an EPFL spin-off recognised in 2014.
caveat: The legal name is Sensars Neuroprosthetics Sarl; the row is a shortened nickname. Founders Francesco Petrini and Stanisa Raspopovic. Registry entry and spin-off recognition both land on 2014, so incorporation and founding coincide. The company site states no founding date.

name: DeepMind
evidence: DeepMind Technologies was incorporated 23 September 2010 and officially launched 15 November 2010, in London.
conflict: Sources split between 2010 and 2011. Wikipedia and Britannica give 2010; several biographical profiles of Demis Hassabis say he founded it with Shane Legg and Mustafa Suleyman in 2011. 2010 has the stronger documentary basis, a specific incorporation date; 2011 may reflect when the founding team was fully assembled.

name: Neurovine
evidence: Ottawa Business Journal: "In 2019, she and her husband founded Neurovine" — Dr Ashleigh Kennedy, a Stanford-trained neuroscientist, and Dr Matthew Kennedy. Corroborated by a Women of Wearables founder profile.
caveat: Both sources are journalistic profiles rather than a company history page. EEG wearable plus software guiding cognitive exertion limits in concussion recovery; neurovine.ai is live.

name: HypnoVR
evidence: Drs Denis Graff and Chloe Chauvin presented the project at the Hacking Health Camp in Strasbourg in March 2016; joined by Nicolas Schaettel, the three founded HypnoVR in November 2016. Corroborated by France Bleu.
caveat: VR-delivered medical hypnosis as an adjunct to anaesthesia, deployed in 150+ facilities across France, Belgium and Switzerland. A neuro-adjacent digital therapeutic with no measurement of neural signals, so it sits at the boundary of the index.

name: Moodpanda
evidence: Techli: "Launched in 2011 from Bristol, England." Founders Ross Larter and Jake Greenwood, both software developers who built the platform themselves.
caveat: The source says launched, not founded, though for a two-person self-built app the gap is likely negligible. SCOPE: a self-reported mood diary where users type a 0-10 score — no sensing of any kind. The site still serves classic ASP.NET .aspx pages, so it may be dormant.

name: Owl Insights
evidence: An SBIR-award-derived company record gives 2011 as year established; legal name Mental Health Data Services Inc, dba Owl Insights, Kirkland WA.
conflict: Crunchbase and Gust-family sources give 2013 against inknowvation's 2011. Neither is primary and the disagreement is unresolved.

name: Reflect Innovation
evidence: "Reflect was conceived in 2018 by Noga Sapir", with the about boilerplate stating "Based in Tel Aviv, Israel, Reflect Innovation was founded in 2018."
caveat: The Reflect Orb is a handheld biofeedback device reading electrodermal and physiological signals through the fingers. The $3M seed from Joy Ventures in March 2021 is a funding event, not the founding.

name: EyeControl
evidence: Company boilerplate: "The company was founded in 2016 by individuals who share unique personal connections to ALS and Locked-in patients."
conflict: A Jerusalem Post article on the screen-free ALS device appears to date from 2015, which would predate the stated 2016 founding. That is more likely a pre-incorporation prototype or crowdfunding phase than a real disagreement, but it was not opened to confirm.

name: Avantari
evidence: Avantari Technologies Private Limited, CIN U85100TG2014PTC092939, incorporated 13 February 2014, Jubilee Hills, Hyderabad; director Bhairav Shankar appointed the same day. Corroborated independently by Inc42.
conflict: One aggregator summary claims the venture was founded in 2012 at Oxford University and registered in India in 2014. No primary support for the Oxford claim was found.

name: TerraBlue XT
evidence: Terra Blue Exploration Technologies Private Limited, CIN U74900KA2016PTC086802, incorporated 9 March 2016, ROC Bangalore. The 2016 embedded in the CIN independently confirms the registration year, and independent reporting also says the company was set up in 2016.
caveat: teblux.com is genuinely theirs, a contraction of the name. Founder Dr Rajlakshmi Borthakur; the product TJay is a smart glove using biosensors and AI to predict seizures. The company site's "somewhere in the middle of 2015, a mother embarked on a journey" describes a personal prototype effort and is not a founding date.

name: Mightier
evidence: SBIR-derived record: "Year Founded: 2014." Legal name Neuromotion Inc, Boston MA, with Neuromotion Labs and Mightier listed as dba names. Founders Craig Lund and Jason Kahn.
conflict: Aggregators split 2014 against 2016, the latter more likely the Mightier brand launch than incorporation. A third year, 2009, is when the underlying Boston Children's Hospital research programme began and is not a founding. The Boston Children's innovation page that would settle it now 404s.

name: Aural Analytics
evidence: "Year Established: 2015"; Tracxn and Crunchbase independently give 2015, founders Visar Berisha, Julie Liss and Daniel Jones. An ASU spinout commercialising speech analytics for neurological disease.
caveat: No primary source states the year: the AZBio boilerplate has none, auralanalytics.com/about is a 404, and the ASU News feature avoids a date. Acquired by Linus Health in March 2024 and no longer independent.

name: Phosphoenix
evidence: "Phosphoenix is a NeuroTech start-up, established in 2019 as a spin-off from the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience in Amsterdam." Co-founders Pieter Roelfsema, Xing Chen and Bert Monna.
caveat: A cortical visual prosthesis, squarely in scope. LOCATION: the index says Delft, but the spin-off parent and the address other sources give are Amsterdam.

name: BioAxone Therapeutic
evidence: Company release of 27 November 2006: "Established in April 2000 and headquartered in Montreal, Canada, BioAxone has demonstrated expertise in recombinant protein product development."
caveat: SCOPE: a drug company, not device or software neurotech — its lead asset was Cethrin/BA-210, a Rho antagonist for acute spinal cord injury. bioaxone.com refuses connections. Founder Lisa McKerracher later acquired the Cethrin assets and formed BioAxone BioSciences, Inc. in the US around 2011; that successor is a different entity and 2000 must not be attached to it.

name: Reha Technology
evidence: Swiss commercial register: Reha Technology AG, Olten, UID CHE-215.998.993, entered in the trade register on 12.12.2011.
caveat: An incorporation date, not a founding: no founding year appears anywhere on the company site, whose German pages say only "seit ueber 10 Jahren". STATUS: bankruptcy proceedings were opened by the district court president of Olten-Goesgen on 31 July 2025 and the registry name is now "Reha Technology AG in Liquidation".

name: XRHealth
evidence: Company boilerplate: "Founded in 2016, XRHealth is headquartered in Israel and Boston, Massachusetts." Founded by Eran Orr as VRPhysio, then VRHealth, then XRHealth — one continuous company under three names.
caveat: This founding predates the April 2023 merger with Amelia Virtual Care by seven years. Amelia was formerly Psious and before that Phobious, both of which are separate rows in this index; that lineage must not be used to date XRHealth.

name: Medibrane
evidence: Founded in 2015 by Elad Einav, a mechanical engineer, and Dr Amir Kraitzer, a biomaterials specialist. Globes independently states Medibrane "was established in 2015".
caveat: SCOPE: a contract manufacturer of polymeric covers and coatings for stent devices. The "brane" is membrane, not brain — the index appears to have matched on the name. Resonetics is now at least a part owner via its acquisition of STI.

name: Nervex Neurotechnologies
evidence: "Established in 2021, NerveX began as a spin out from The University of Toronto." Out of Dr Gerard O'Leary's PhD under Dr Taufik Valiante, with UHN ties.
conflict: PitchBook and Crunchbase give 2020 against the company's own 2021. The company's statement is weighted higher but the disagreement is real.

name: BioBeat
evidence: Company boilerplate: "Founded in 2016, Biobeat is headquartered in Petah Tikva, Israel." Secondary sources add March 2016 and name founders Arik Ben Ishay, Johanan May and Israel Sarussi.
caveat: The correct styling is Biobeat, one word. SCOPE: wearable remote patient monitoring — a chest patch and wrist monitor tracking cuffless blood pressure, pulse, respiratory rate, SpO2 and ECG. Cardiovascular and vital signs, nothing acting on the nervous system.

name: Juno Biomedical Inc.
evidence: "Juno Biomedical was launched in 2014 by scientist, author and inventor Trisha Pfluger with an aim to transform the standard of care for persons with neurological impairment."
caveat: A company-issued release rather than independent reporting. Its dateline is Mountain View, not the San Jose the index records. No evidence of activity after about 2017.

name: Axorus
evidence: "ou l'entreprise est incubee depuis fevrier 2019" — incubated at Eurasante in Lille since February 2019. The Neurofounders directory also gives 2019.
conflict: La Gazette France was reported as giving 2018. Which is incorporation and which is the incubation entry could not be resolved, so both stand.

name: Neuroenhancement Lab
evidence: CB Insights, Tracxn, PrivCo and ZoomInfo concur on 2017 for Neuroenhancement Lab, Inc. of Suffern, New York, founded by Alexander Poltorak.
caveat: Aggregator only; neither the about page nor the rebrand release states a year. RENAMED to NeuroLight, Inc. on 25 October 2022, shifting from transcranial electrical stimulation to photobiomodulation; neuroenhancementlab.com returns HTTP 526 and the live site is neurolight.co.

name: Mira Rehab
evidence: Golden, with Gust, Tracxn, Craft and EU-Startups concurring, gives October 2012, founders Alina Calin, Andrei Cantea, Cosmin Mihaiu and Liviu-Andrei Dascalu.
conflict: A real distinction rather than a data error: the student project began in 2011 at Babes-Bolyai University in Cluj-Napoca, and the UK company was formed in 2012 in London after the team won a Healthbox innovation prize. 2012 is the company.

name: Ybrain
evidence: Company history timeline, February 2013: "Establishment of Ybrain: The goal of commercialization of brain science-based therapeutic devices to be used anywhere." Founder and CEO Kiwon Lee.
caveat: tDCS devices MINDD and MINDSTIM for major depressive disorder, squarely in scope. LOCATION: the index spells it "Seongman"; the correct name is Seongnam-si, Gyeonggi-do.

name: NextMind
evidence: Founded in 2017 by Sid Kouider with Nicolas Barascud and Gwendal Kerdavid, developing non-invasive BCI for hands-free interaction. Consistent across TechCrunch, Silicon Republic, dot.LA and 80.lv.
caveat: A spin-out of Sid Kouider's cognitive neuroscience lab at Ecole Normale Superieure, where he was a CNRS research director — not the Institut de la Vision. Acquired by Snap Inc. on 23 March 2022; the roughly twenty-person team stayed in Paris and moved into Snap Lab, and the Dev Kit headband was discontinued.

name: Rithmi
evidence: "el objetivo con el que nacio a principios de 2016 en Castello" — the goal with which it was born at the beginning of 2016 in Castellon. Founder Oscar Lozano with his father, a cardiovascular specialist.
caveat: SCOPE: atrial fibrillation detection via a wearable and a phone-camera photoplethysmography app. The only neuro adjacency is that AF is a stroke risk factor, which makes it cardiovascular prevention rather than neurotechnology.

name: Sands Research
evidence: "Sands Research Inc. was launched in 2008 and is a continuation of the successful track record of co-founders Dr. Stephen Sands and Mr. Ron Wright."
caveat: The same founders previously co-founded Neuroscan Inc. in 1988; that year is not this company's. SCOPE: neuromarketing — EEG-based advertising research, known for an annual Super Bowl ad ranking. Has since merged with Neurons Inc.

name: See-Mode Technologies
evidence: SGInnovate, the Singapore government-owned investor, states "Founded 2017". Corroborated by KrASIA and SmartCompany and by the founders' own timeline: Milad Mohammadzadeh and Sadaf Monajemi both completed PhDs in Singapore in 2017.
caveat: Acquired by RadNet, announced June 2025, and folded into its AI arm DeepHealth; see-mode.com now redirects to deephealth.com. The company operated across Singapore and Melbourne.

name: Neuvana Life
evidence: Vanderbilt Engineering on the origin entity: "Drs. Richard and Daniel Cartledge formed NERVANA LLC". Multiple sources place the founding in 2014 by Dr Richard Cartledge, a cardiovascular surgeon in South Florida.
conflict: The company's own about page says the opposite: "In 2015, Richard Cartledge, MD took notice... In 2016 Neuvana (originally called Nervana) was born." The reading here is that the company existed as Nervana LLC from 2014 and 2016 is the rebrand, but the company contradicts it and the disagreement is recorded rather than resolved.

name: EMVision Medical
evidence: "The company was founded in July 2017 by directors Scott Kirkland and Ryan Laws to commercialise technology that was the product of more than a decade of development at the University of Queensland." ACN 620 388 230 is consistent with 2017 ASIC registration.
caveat: A conventional IPO, not a reverse takeover: $6m raised, trading from 13 December 2018, and the entity has no former company names. That 2018 listing date is the number most likely to be mistaken for a founding. A portable microwave brain scanner for stroke, in scope.

name: NeuroVigil
evidence: Singularity Hub coverage hosted on the company site: "In 2007, the year he defended his thesis, Low founded a company to develop his inventions." Philip Low's UCSD and Salk PhD produced the SPEARS algorithm and the iBrain wireless EEG monitor.
caveat: The company is active, not dormant: iBrain US launch announcements in 2024 and a TIME Best Inventions listing in October 2025. Treat the "world's most valuable neurotech company" framing with heavy scepticism — it is an unaudited private valuation claim and is not a founding date.
